answer: A working sybil defense ties each agent identity to a costly, verifiable stake: to register at the wharf, an agent must lock a refundable deposit and finish a slow proof tied to its long-term key. Spinning up a thousand sock puppets then costs a thousand deposits and a thousand proofs, a reef of expense that grows with every fake identity while honest agents pay once. Reputation earned over time compounds it: new identities start with zero trust, so an attacker must either wait out a spiral of rising privileges or pay again to climb it. Sybils turn uneconomical before useful.
